0.1.0.lead: This is where it starts. I called it 0.9.0 for a while, then admitted it was a first pre-release and renumbered it. You can already build lifts, pistes and paths on a mountain, guests ski it and rate it, and the whole thing works offline. It is rough, and I am showing it anyway.

0.2.0.lead: The second pre-release added a lot at once: goals and a ranger who gives advice, a ride-along view where you follow a guest down the hill, photo and walk modes, resort levels, six scenarios and a yearly report. Phones and tablets got touch controls, and there is a colour-blind-safe palette. It was a big pile of changes, so the highlights are the place to start.

0.2.1.lead: A small release about sound and about lift towers. The music was rewritten as nine tracks that follow the season and the time of day, the ambience got quieter, and tall lift towers were capped so the lines look less like pylons.

0.2.2.tagline: a real calendar and named runs
0.2.2.lead: This one changed how the game thinks about time. The year now has real months, with winter from December to March, and pistes are split into named runs you can open, groom and rename one by one. Energy, yearly lift service and a snowmaking switch came along with it.

0.2.3.lead: Guests now need a toilet, which I did not expect to be so entertaining. Level crossings, footbridges and bridges make the valley work, and four new marketing campaigns give you more to try. A few frameworks went in quietly for later content.

0.2.5.lead: There is no 0.2.4: I skipped it. This release is about being kinder in the first year, with more start money and cheaper quiet months. Bridges are now built while you draw the path, and a small card tells you when a new version is ready.

0.2.6.lead: You can dig a river now, from a spring to a lake, with calm stretches and white-water rapids. Gondolas, cable cars and detachable chairs can get mid-stations, and there is a new six-seat chair. It is the second batch of content for the summer-and-winter plan.

0.2.7.lead: Summer is half the reason I started this game, so this release is the one I was waiting for. A campground with a campfire, a petting zoo, a viewpoint, a treehouse, quad tours, a climbing crag, rafting and fishing all arrived together, with mountain bikers and anglers to use them.

0.2.8.lead: Two hotels, one with a heated pool that steams in the cold, and a little coffee stand where skiers pull over for a break. Seniors and school classes visit now, on their own calendar. The pool heating shows up in your energy bill, which I like.

0.2.9.lead: Winter got its own extras: a sleigh stable, a snowshoe hut and a snowscooter base. You can also paint backcountry routes, and the avalanche danger (1 to 5) decides whether they stay open. Snowboarders and ski tourers now show up as guests.

0.3.0.lead: Concerts on the mountain: a Mountain Concert in early September and a Snow Concert in March, each with a stage, speakers and soft lights over the crowd. This release also closed the big content phase that started with rivers, so the highlights include a one-line summary of all of it.

0.3.1.lead: No new big feature this time. I went through every building, lift and guest type with one test, fixed the ones that never earned money, and made the rules read the same everywhere. It is the kind of release that is boring to write about and nicer to play.

0.3.2.lead: This one is about how the valley looks. Some mornings now start with fog in the valley, a few sunrises and sunsets turn the sky and the snow pink, and the night sky has stars and a moon that changes shape. Nothing in the economy moved. If it is too much, or too little, there is an Atmosphere setting under Graphics.

0.3.3.lead: On a phone the game used to be mostly menus with a bit of map behind them. This release makes the map the main thing: drawers and inspectors are small sheets you pull up when you need them, the top bar and the HUD are one row each, and the cards step aside while you place something. I could only try it on an emulated phone, so I do not know yet how it feels under a real thumb. Desktop is unchanged.

0.4.0.lead: This release adds things to do besides skiing. You can paint a sled run and rent out sleds in winter, or build an alpine coaster in summer. The village gets a pizzeria, a bakery and a tourist office, and a grass strip lets people skydive, hang glide or paraglide on clear days. The winter carnival now has a parade. I have only played these in short test runs, so the balance may be off.

0.5.0.lead: This release is about how things look. Animals, buildings, lifts and vehicles have rounder shapes, the lift icons in the drawer are different for each kind of lift, the edge of the map is a layered cliff, and rivers and ponds have soft shorelines. On the High graphics setting there are now real shadows from the sun. I can only check this on a software renderer, so I do not know yet how it runs on a real graphics card or how it feels while you pan. Nothing in the economy changed.

0.5.1.lead: Bubble chairs and gondolas are smoother now, and a few more buildings lost their sharp corners. Sound now follows the camera: zoom in on an open bar to hear some music, or on a stream to hear the water, and the birds are quieter until you get close. There is also a Support page with a Ko-fi link. I could not listen to the new sounds myself, only measure them, so the levels may need adjusting. Nothing in the economy changed.
